articles.title: Music Assistant syncs Hue lights without a Hue bridge
articles.dek: An experimental connection links compatible lamps on Home Assistant’s ZHA network to the music.
body: Music Assistant adds an experimental way to make Hue lights follow music without a Hue bridge. The Hue Lights Sync setup connects through Home Assistant’s ZHA Zigbee integration, provided ZHA uses Ziggurat and the Music Assistant Home Assistant plugin is connected.

The setup lists Hue lamps that support Zigbee entertainment and turns a chosen group into one light player. Gradient lamps support up to three zones. Only one Zigbee light stream runs at a time: starting another restores the previous group’s lighting state.
The direct Zigbee work reported on November 10 now has a Music Assistant setup path. Marcel van der Veldt tested it with two Hue lamps on a live ZHA network.

pullRequests.title: Sync Hue lamps on Home Assistant's ZHA without a Hue bridge
Describe both Hue Lights Sync backends in the setup notes

articles.title: Piper accepts larger custom voices and keeps them in backups
articles.dek: The Home Assistant app removes an upload limit and separates personal voice models from replaceable downloads.
body: Piper’s Home Assistant app removes a 16 MiB upload limit that rejected many custom voice models. A 60.6 MB model that failed before completed successfully in the contributor’s test.

Custom uploads get their own storage directory, separate from voices downloaded from the catalog. Backups keep uploaded voices and fine-tunes while excluding replaceable catalog downloads. A custom voice also takes precedence over a catalog voice with the same name.
WhoCares1337 contributes the upload fix in their first contribution to the app’s repository; Michael Hansen handles the storage separation.

articles.title: CarPlay puts the queue and favorites within reach
articles.dek: Music Assistant adds Up Next, audiobook chapter selection and a heart button to its car interface.
body: Music Assistant’s CarPlay interface adds an Up Next button to Now Playing. It opens the current queue and, for an audiobook, its chapter list. Selecting an item starts it or jumps to the chapter, then returns to Now Playing.

A heart button adds or removes a track from favorites. While listening to radio it saves the song on air; the button is absent for long-form content and accounts without permission to change the library.
CarPlay’s home rows also follow the visibility and ordering chosen in the app, keeping the car view aligned with those preferences.

articles.title: Home Assistant reverses its camera startup shortcut
articles.dek: Further testing restores parallel video connections and limits retries when talkback cannot connect.
body: Home Assistant starts a camera’s fallback video alongside the WebRTC connection used for talkback again. That reverses the strategy described in yesterday’s edition: remembering a successful WebRTC connection no longer makes the fallback wait twelve seconds, and the browser stops filtering the connection-server list.

Wendelin’s follow-up testing found that those shortcuts did not solve slow starts. Relay setup in go2rtc with Home Assistant Cloud connection servers remains the suspected bottleneck. The player gives up sooner on an initial WebRTC connection that cannot start, while retaining microphone handover and the last visible frame during reconnection.

pullRequests.title: Revert camera ICE server filter and WebRTC-first memory

articles.title: Z-Wave shutters get more accurate identities
articles.dek: Some cover automations need updated device classes, and redundant slat entities can be removed.
body: Home Assistant classifies supported Fibaro, Shelly, Aeotec and ZVIDAR motor controllers as shutters, blinds, gates or shades according to their device and operating mode. A gate can consequently appear as a garage door through HomeKit, Alexa or Google, instead of being classified as a window.

Owners who use the old window device class in cover triggers, conditions, templates or dashboards need to update those references. Some Fibaro FGR-223 and Shelly Wave Shutter configurations also stop creating a separate slat cover: the main cover provides tilt control, and the leftover slat entity can be removed.

articles.title: ESPHome controls BrizLabs two-wire light strings
articles.dek: A new component brings compatible decorative strings into ESPHome, with colors and effects applied across repeating zones.
body: ESPHome adds control for BrizLabs light strings that carry color commands over the same two wires as their power. Makers building compatible ESP32 firmware can use ESPHome light effects, including rainbows, wipes and twinkles, with these strings.

The component controls repeating color zones rather than every LED individually. Tyler tests it on a BrizLabs 200-LED controller built around an ESP32-C2. This is Tyler’s first contribution to ESPHome.

articles.title: Music Assistant jumps straight to a letter
articles.dek: An optional alphabet rail shortens the journey through long artist, album and track libraries.
body: Music Assistant adds an alphabet rail for jumping through artist, album and track libraries. Tapping or dragging to a letter takes the list to that part of the collection instead of requiring a long scroll.

The option starts off and can be enabled in Settings → User Interface → Preferences. It follows the current library filters and works with name or sort-name ordering, including reverse order. Search results and other sort orders do not show the letter index.

articles.title: YAML dashboards need explicit configuration
articles.dek: The old top-level dashboard mode stops selecting a YAML dashboard.
body: Home Assistant removes the deprecated lovelace: mode: yaml setting. Leaving it in place no longer selects ui-lovelace.yaml: Home Assistant logs an error and falls back to a dashboard managed through the interface.

To keep a YAML dashboard, configure it explicitly under lovelace.dashboards.lovelace with mode: yaml and filename: ui-lovelace.yaml. Installations that also define dashboard resources in YAML need resource_mode: yaml. The source includes the complete replacement configuration.

articles.title: Home Assistant installation works without US keyboard shortcuts
articles.dek: Arrow keys and Enter replace letter-dependent choices in the live USB console.
body: Home Assistant’s live USB installer can be operated throughout with arrow keys and Enter. That avoids a trap for non-US keyboards: the console’s US keymap can turn the expected shortcut or typed erase confirmation into different characters.
The confirmation screen initially selects Go Back, so repeatedly pressing Enter does not approve an erase. Escape returns to the previous screen, while existing letter shortcuts remain available.

articles.title: ESPHome makes power monitors signal when a limit is crossed
articles.dek: INA226 sensors can assert a hardware alert when voltage or power crosses a configured threshold.
body: ESPHome lets an INA226 power monitor signal through its alert pin when voltage or power crosses a chosen threshold. Wiring that pin to a digital input gives a maker’s device a signal it can use in an automation, alongside the sensor’s regular measurements.
The alert can remain active until explicitly cleared, or release when the condition ends. 马诗旻 adds the capability in a first contribution to ESPHome, with accompanying documentation.

articles.title: Music Assistant proposes an optional community catalog
articles.dek: Community-maintained integrations would have a separate distribution route controlled by an administrator.
body: Music Assistant proposes a community catalog for integrations maintained outside its server repository. Maintainers would publish from their own repositories through a registry owned by the project, and the catalog would appear in the app only after an administrator enables it.

The plan covers admission rules, release checks, installation and moving providers out of the server. It extends the distinction between team and community maintenance introduced earlier this month into a separate way to distribute those integrations.

articles.title: Tuya circuit breakers expose their fault warnings
articles.dek: Supported devices report leakage current and individual problem states.
body: Home Assistant turns supported Tuya circuit-breaker fault reports into individual diagnostic sensors, so each warning has its own state. The same breaker category gains a leakage-current reading in milliamps.
The available entities depend on the measurements and fault states each device reports. These are readings from the breaker, rather than a new protection function in Home Assistant.

articles.title: Portainer makes slow disk measurements optional
articles.dek: Existing disk-space sensors are disabled too, and can be re-enabled if needed.
body: Home Assistant disables Portainer disk-space sensors by default, including existing ones, so a slow Docker disk-usage request does not hold up the rest of an endpoint’s updates. Owners who need those readings can re-enable the relevant entities.
Volume disk measurements move from the normal 60-second update cycle to the 30-minute disk-usage cycle. The integration requests disk usage only for endpoints with enabled disk sensors.

articles.title: ESPHome directs messages to individual devices on shared links
articles.dek: A shared serial or radio connection can carry separate conversations between configured ESPHome devices.
body: ESPHome gives makers a way to address individual devices over a shared connection such as an RS485 bus or LoRa radio. Each device can accept messages meant for it while ignoring other traffic, and a single link can maintain a separate conversation with each configured peer.
Messages that exceed the connection’s packet limit are split and reassembled at the receiving device. Makers configure the participating ESPHome devices and their addresses.
